messages:
PagerBot: PagerDuty SEV-1 ▸ streaming-decode-gpu-oom spike on cluster decode-prod-us-west-2 — 14% request drops in last 120s. Paging @Nina (oncall).

Nina (oncall): I’m awake, seeing alerts. Confirming impact: which routes/models?

PagerBot: Affected endpoints: /v1/stream/generate (gptx-decode-v1), some traffic routed to fallback slow-models. CUDA OOM stack seen on decode nodes 3/5 in pool decode-prod-03.

Samir: logs show repeated cudaErrorIllegalInstruction followed by OOM on small-batch decodes. Likely runaway generation / max_tokens mismatch on a client.

Elaine: Customer CS reports increased 5xx and partial streams. Marco, any customer tickets?

Marco (CS): Two mid-enterprise customers have flagged missing tokens in streams and dropped responses. I’ve opened tickets and asked for ETA for mitigation comms.

Nina (oncall): Quick mitigation plan: 1) route traffic off decode-prod-03 2) enable model-variant fallback to quantized-v2 for low-priority traffic 3) throttle high token-rate clients via gateway. Who can execute?

Ops SRE: I’ll spin up replacement nodes and cordon decode-prod-03. Running: `kubectl cordon node/decode-prod-03` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets node/decode-prod-03`

Samir: On router: setting per-route max_output_tokens=512 and enabling soft cap enforcement for /v1/stream/generate to prevent runaway. Command: `rtctl route update /v1/stream/generate --max-output 512 --soft-enforce true`

Elaine: I’ll push a temporary heuristic to drop requests with token_budget > 2000 at the edge for 10 minutes.

Nina (oncall): Also flip fallback policy to prefer cpu-safe fallback for requests from impacted customers to avoid further GPU OOMs. `route-policy set fallback decode-prod-us-west-2 -> cpu-serve-v1`

Ops SRE: Replacement nodes booting. Observed container crash loops on decode-prod-03 containers with logs: ```cudaMemcpyAsync failed: out of memory
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'```

Samir: That aligns with a client sending huge max_tokens + streaming loop. Telemetry shows a spike from client token-rate header X-Client-Token-Rate: 3.2k/s from IP range 18.44.0.0/16.

Nina (oncall): Set temporary IP-level rate limit for that prefix to 200 rps. `rtctl ipblock add 18.44.0.0/16 --rps 200 --reason "OOM surge source"`

Marco (CS): Notifying affected customers: sending short update: "We detected streaming failures and are routing your requests to safe fallback while we remediate; expect full service in ~15-30m."

Elaine: Metrics trending: GPU mem pressure dropping after cordon and route changes. Request drops down from 14% to ~3% in 8 minutes.

Samir: Follow-up: we should add a decoder-side soft cap that aborts sequences when KV cache growth > threshold to avoid similar OOMs. Filing a backlog ticket.

Ops SRE: decode-prod-03 recovered after restart and eviction; keeping cordoned for deeper postmortem. Will capture `/var/log/engine/` and coredump.

Nina (oncall): Oncall notes: applied edge rate limit, route max_tokens cap, node cordon/drain, fallback to cpu route, customer comms. Status: degraded -> partial service restored.

Marco (CS): Customers acknowledged mitigation, asked for RCA and whether data was lost. I told them no persisted data lost but some streaming responses were truncated; full RCA to follow.

Samir: Quick debugging snippet for triage: `grep -E "OOM|cuda" /var/log/engine/*.log | tail -n 50` shows repeated kernel allocation failures after a long decode session.

Nina (oncall): Handing off to SRE for postmortem and to infra for long-term fixes. Leaving a list of action items in incident tracker. If anything regresses, re-paging. :white_check_mark:

Ops SRE: Acknowledged, taking over. Will include network throttles, decoder soft caps, and model-variant autoswitch in follow-up.

Marco (CS): Sending customer follow-up now. Will attach status update and expected RCA timeline (24–48h).

Nina (oncall): Closing oncall shift, incident state -> monitoring. Thanks everyone. :heart:
